LiveHttpConcurrencyTests.test_http_mutat.obsolete: Mutations no longer serialize in the process (#1331): each commits in its own PostgreSQL transaction, and tests/pg/test_http_concurrency.py::ConcurrentHttpTests.test_unrelated_mutations_run_at_once shows two running at once.

LiveHttpConcurrencyTests.test_http_backu.note: The PostgreSQL backup is written by the worker from one snapshot, so reads and writes both continue while it runs. The /api/processing-files?rescan=1 mutation the SQLite test also held off is the legacy inbox scan, which PostgreSQL does not have.

LiveHttpConcurrencyTests.test_http_resto.note: A PostgreSQL restore rebinds nothing: it replaces the Library's rows in one transaction under the maintenance lock, and the old epoch is fenced (docs/postgresql-architecture.md §7.4).

LiveHttpConcurrencyTests.test_sqlite_thr.note: SQLite connections are owned by one thread; each PostgreSQL request borrows its own pooled connection, so two reads run in the facade at the same time.

LiveHttpConcurrencyTests.test_partial_mu.obsolete: There is no process-local mutation scope to hold since #1331; a mutation's body is read before its PostgreSQL command starts, as tests/pg/test_postgres_library_start.py shows for a stalled restore body.
